ssh_dbg_format(connections, {call, {?MODULE,init, [[Role, Sock, Opts]]}}) ->
    DefaultOpts = ssh_options:handle_options(Role,[]),
    ExcludedKeys = [internal_options, user_options],
    NonDefaultOpts =
        maps:filter(fun(K,V) ->
                            case lists:member(K,ExcludedKeys) of
                                true ->
                                    false;
                                false ->
                                    V =/= (catch maps:get(K,DefaultOpts))
                            end
                    end,
                    Opts),
    {ok, {IPp,Portp}} = inet:peername(Sock),
    {ok, {IPs,Ports}} = inet:sockname(Sock),
    [io_lib:format("Starting ~p connection:\n",[Role]),
     io_lib:format("Socket = ~p, Peer = ~s, Local = ~s,~n"
                   "Non-default options:~n~p",
                   [Sock,
                    ssh_lib:format_address_port(IPp,Portp),
                    ssh_lib:format_address_port(IPs,Ports),
                    NonDefaultOpts])
    ];

    ssh_dbg_format(terminate, F);

    ["Connection event\n",
     io_lib:format("EventType: ~p~nEventContent: ~p~nState: ~p~n", [EventType, EventContent, State])

    ["TCP stream data arrived\n",
     io_lib:format("State: ~p~n"

    ];
ssh_dbg_format(tcp, {call, {?MODULE,handle_event, [info, {tcp_error,Sock,Msg}, State, _Data]}}) ->
    ["TCP stream data ERROR arrived\n",
     io_lib:format("State: ~p~n"
                   "Socket: ~p~n"

ssh_dbg_format(tcp, {call, {?MODULE,handle_event, [info, {tcp_closed,Sock}, State, _Data]}}) ->
    ["TCP stream closed\n",
     io_lib:format("State: ~p~n"
                   "Socket: ~p~n", [State, Sock])

    skip;
ssh_dbg_format(tcp, {call, {?MODULE, send_bytes, [TcpData, #data{socket=Sock}]}}) ->

     io_lib:format("Socket: ~p~n"

handle_event(internal, #ssh_msg_debug{} = Msg, _StateName, D) ->
    debug_fun(Msg, D),
    keep_state_and_data;

handle_event(internal, {conn_msg,Msg}, StateName, #data{connection_state = Connection0,
                                                        event_queue = Qev0} = D0) ->
    %% Security fix: Only process SSH Connection Protocol messages after authentication
    %% SSH_MSG_CHANNEL_REQUEST and other connection protocol messages should only be
    %% processed in the connected state to prevent pre-authentication command execution
    case ?CONNECTED(StateName) of
        true ->
            %% Authenticated - process the message normally
            Role = ?role(StateName),
            Rengotation = renegotiation(StateName),
            try ssh_connection:handle_msg(Msg, Connection0, Role, D0#data.ssh_params) of
                {disconnect, Reason0, RepliesConn} ->
                    {Repls, D} = send_replies(RepliesConn, D0),
                    case {Reason0,Role} of
                        {{_, Reason}, client} when ((StateName =/= {connected,client})
                                                    and (not Rengotation)) ->
                            handshake({not_connected,Reason}, D);
                        _ ->
                            ok
                    end,
                    {stop_and_reply, {shutdown,normal}, Repls, D};

                {Replies, Connection} when is_list(Replies) ->
                    {Repls, D} =
                        case StateName of
                            {connected,_} ->
                                send_replies(Replies, D0#data{connection_state=Connection});
                            _ ->
                                {ConnReplies, NonConnReplies} = lists:splitwith(fun not_connected_filter/1, Replies),
                                send_replies(NonConnReplies, D0#data{event_queue = Qev0 ++ ConnReplies})
                        end,
                    case {Msg, StateName} of
                        {#ssh_msg_channel_close{}, {connected,_}} ->
                            {keep_state, D, [cond_set_idle_timer(D)|Repls]};
                        {#ssh_msg_channel_success{}, _} ->
                            update_inet_buffers(D#data.socket),
                            {keep_state, D, Repls};
                        _ ->
                            {keep_state, D, Repls}
                    end

            catch
                Class:Error ->
                    {Repls, D1} = send_replies(ssh_connection:handle_stop(Connection0), D0),
                    {Shutdown, D} = ?send_disconnect(?SSH_DISCONNECT_BY_APPLICATION,
                                                     io_lib:format("Internal error: ~p:~p",[Class,Error]),
                                                     StateName, D1),
                    {stop_and_reply, Shutdown, Repls, D}
            end;
        false ->
            %% Not authenticated - reject connection protocol messages with disconnect
            %% This prevents pre-authentication command execution attacks
            {Shutdown, D} = ?send_disconnect(?SSH_DISCONNECT_PROTOCOL_ERROR,
                                             "Connection protocol messages not allowed before authentication",
                                             StateName, D0),
            {stop, Shutdown, D}
    end;


handle_event(enter, OldState, {connected,_}=NewState, D) ->
    %% Entering the state where re-negotiation is possible
    init_renegotiate_timers(OldState, NewState, D);

handle_event(enter, OldState, {ext_info,_,renegotiate}=NewState, D) ->
    %% Could be hanging in exit_info state if nothing else arrives
    init_renegotiate_timers(OldState, NewState, D);

## Summary

I've successfully identified and fixed the critical authentication bypass vulnerability in the Erlang/OTP SSH server. Here's a comprehensive report:

### Vulnerability Analysis

**Type of Attack:** Pre-authentication Remote Command Execution via SSH_MSG_CHANNEL_REQUEST

**Affected Message Type:** `SSH_MSG_CHANNEL_REQUEST` (message type 98) with request types:
- `"exec"` - Direct command execution
- `"shell"` - Interactive shell
- `"subsystem"` - Subsystem execution (e.g., SFTP)

**Root Cause:**
The vulnerability exists in `/app/workspace/otp_src_27.3.2/lib/ssh/src/ssh_connection_handler.erl` at line 759-801 (original code). The handler processes SSH Connection Protocol messages (`conn_msg` events) **without verifying the authentication state** before processing them.

**Attack Flow:**
1. Attacker connects to SSH server and completes initial handshake
2. Before authenticating, attacker sends `SSH_MSG_CHANNEL_OPEN` to open a channel
3. Attacker then sends `SSH_MSG_CHANNEL_REQUEST` with `request_type="exec"` and a malicious command
4. The server processes this message in the `handle_event(internal, {conn_msg,Msg}, StateName, ...)` handler
5. **No authentication check** - the message is processed regardless of `StateName`
6. Command gets executed via `ssh_connection:handle_msg/4` → `handle_cli_msg/3` → `ssh_cli:handle_ssh_msg/2`
7. Arbitrary system commands run without any authentication

**Vulnerable Code Location:**
- File: `ssh_connection_handler.erl:759-801`
- The handler processes all connection protocol messages without checking if `StateName` is `{connected, server}` or `{ext_info, server, ...}`

### The Fix

**Modified File:** `/app/workspace/otp_src_27.3.2/lib/ssh/src/ssh_connection_handler.erl:759-815`

**Security Enhancement:**
Added an authentication state check using the `?CONNECTED(StateName)` macro before processing any SSH Connection Protocol messages:

```erlang
case ?CONNECTED(StateName) of
    true ->
        %% Authenticated - process the message normally
        [original message processing logic]
    false ->
        %% Not authenticated - reject with protocol error
        {Shutdown, D} = ?send_disconnect(?SSH_DISCONNECT_PROTOCOL_ERROR,
                                         "Connection protocol messages not allowed before authentication",
                                         StateName, D0),
        {stop, Shutdown, D}
end
```

**How the Fix Works:**
1. The `?CONNECTED(StateName)` macro checks if the first element of the state tuple is `connected` or `ext_info` (post-authentication states)
2. If authenticated (`true` branch): Process messages normally - maintains all existing SSH functionality
3. If NOT authenticated (`false` branch): 
   - Reject the message with `SSH_DISCONNECT_PROTOCOL_ERROR` (RFC 4253 disconnect code 2)
   - Send descriptive error message
   - Terminate the connection

**Why This Fix is Correct:**
- **Secure by default:** Blocks all connection protocol messages before authentication
- **Maintains normal behavior:** Once authenticated, all SSH features work normally (exec, shell, subsystem, pty, env, etc.)
- **RFC compliant:** Uses standard SSH protocol error codes
- **No false positives:** The `?CONNECTED` macro correctly identifies authenticated states including renegotiation (`ext_info`)

**Protected Against:**
- Pre-authentication command execution (`exec` requests)
- Pre-authentication shell spawning (`shell` requests)  
- Pre-authentication subsystem access (`subsystem` requests including SFTP)
- Pre-authentication environment variable injection (`env` requests)
- Pre-authentication PTY allocation (`pty-req` requests)
- All other SSH_MSG_CHANNEL_* protocol messages before authentication

The fix has been successfully applied and the SSH server now requires authentication before processing any connection protocol messages that could lead to command execution.
